reason: The FACT is confirmed, but the finding adds almost nothing new, and the check it proposes does not work. (1) Code: kaggle 2.2.4 kernels_output (l.6640-6743) drops the parsed version. ApiListKernelSessionOutputRequest does have a version_label field, but read-only probes on amanatar/optimized-biohub-max-score gave HTTP 404 for version_label '1'/'4'/'10' and HTTP 403 for kernel_slug 'slug/N'. There is no API route to one version's output. kernels pull does honour N (l.6541). (2) Not new: P4b(c) (CONTEXT 13:27Z) already says 'The CLI pulls and outputs the LATEST version only'. The plan check this round already has --file-pattern (PC12: 16 s vs 216 s) and the early author fetch (PC12 429 item, action 2). (3) The proposed detector is broken. For amanatar, get_kernel metadata reads current_version_number = 5 and last_run_time 23 Sep 20:45Z. But a no-version pull returns the v10 source (it contains the 30600 override and '# v6: validator ON'). The output listing serves the v10 ERROR session (PapermillExecutionError at In [11]; kernels status ERROR), and that session still includes submission.csv and run_stats.csv. So current_version_number does not move when a newer version errors, and probably not while one runs. Re-reading it would miss exactly the race the finding targets. (4) The harm is fail-safe or harmless. The author CSV feeds only the per-clip node-count gate, plus the informational author-log check in R12RT-4. A drifted CSV either disagrees with our dummy (FAIL, no port: a false negative) or agrees (M+1 behaves like M, which is harmless). R5 runtime uses the x138 ledger family, not the author log. The race needs the author to push in a window of minutes, times P(trigger) 5-15%. (5) Rules: this is procedure only. There is no mechanism and no kernel change, so there is nothing to check for byte-identity or fail-safety, and it needs no OK. The effect is below noise.
fix: Mechanical hygiene for the E10 command sequence, replacing the finding's check; no OK needed. (a) At the trigger: record sha256 of the pulled .ipynb (S1) and `kaggle kernels status <author>/<slug>` (must be COMPLETE; RUNNING, QUEUED or ERROR means a newer session exists: notify and wait or restart from the trigger). (b) Fetch the author output once, right after the static gate, with `kaggle kernels output <author>/<slug> -p _dl/<name> --file-pattern '^(submission\.csv|run_stats\.csv)$' -o`. Do not append /N: it is silently ignored, and a version_label is not a version number (404). (c) Straight after the fetch, re-pull the source into a temp folder, require sha256 == S1, and re-run kernels status == COMPLETE. On any change, discard the author CSV and restart from the trigger (P4b(c): a newer version means the scored-latest condition must be re-read on the page). (d) Do NOT use get_kernel current_version_number or last_run_time as the drift detector: measured on amanatar, they stay at v5 / 23 Sep while v10 is the served session. The version number for --version comes from the notebook page ('Version M of M') via the browser, as P4c(7) already requires. (e) An author CSV that comes from an ERROR session can exist (amanatar v10 has one), so status COMPLETE is required, not just file presence.
realistic_gain: About 0 (below 1e-4 P(bronze)). It needs a trigger (5-15%) plus an author push inside a window of minutes. Even then the gate fails safe (no port) or passes harmlessly. It does not affect finals #37 + #38. The only practical value is fewer false-negative gate FAILs and a clearer audit trail, and the fix costs about 1 minute (one re-pull and one status call) at a trigger.
